source.episode_title: Why One Red Cord Survived the Fall of Jericho
source.anchor_kjv: Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father’s household, home unto thee.
source.thread: Faith, not a past, was what saved Rahab
source.hook_line: When Jericho fell, one family walked out alive.
source.spoken_script: When Jericho fell, one family walked out alive. Her name was Rahab. She lived in Jericho's wall. The Bible calls her a prostitute. Two spies came from God's people, Israel. She hid them, because she believed in their God. They told her: hang a red cord in your window, and your family will be safe. Israel marched. The people shouted. And "the wall fell down flat". Rahab and her family were spared. The cord was the sign. Trusting the promise saved her. A book of the Bible, Hebrews, says it in two words: "By faith". She is named in the family line of Jesus, God's Son, who "taketh away the sin of the world". Rahab could not stop a wall. She tied one cord to a promise. Tie your trust to Jesus, and bring everyone you love inside.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS
- Anchor quote: matches Joshua 2:18 KJV. No change.
- Title: curiosity gap is true to the text (cord = sign, Joshua 2:18; faith, Hebrews 11:31). Not clickbait.
- Doctrine: "The cord was the sign. Hebrews says what saved her: faith" matches the video and Heb 11:31. Matthew names her in Jesus's line (Matt 1:5): accurate. The cord-as-blood reading is not in the metadata. Good.
- CTA: "bring everyone you love inside" is an invitation. It does not promise anyone's salvation.
- TikTok/Instagram: hook is in the first line. Fine.
